<p align="center">
<a href="https://arena.dualmindlab.tech"><picture><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/harshbhx/harshbhx/main/assets/arena-story-dark.svg"><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)" srcset="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/harshbhx/harshbhx/main/assets/arena-story-light.svg"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/harshbhx/harshbhx/main/assets/arena-story-dark.svg" alt="Cover story, DualMind Labs: DualMind Arena, live. Blind, head-to-head AI model evaluation. Public AI benchmarks are easy to game: cherry-picked prompts, brand bias, results nobody can audit. Two models answer the same real prompt with their names hidden; the community votes before the identities are revealed, and the votes feed a live leaderboard. Box score: 5,000+ requests absorbed in one traffic spike (Bots + real users; Cloudflare CDN took the load before it reached the origin.); #1 on Google for “DualMind Labs” (dualmindlab.tech); Real-time login anomaly detection (IP capture, risk scoring and an email alert to the account owner on every suspicious event.); Docs full user documentation, published (docs.dualmindlab.tech). Next: Expanding from model evaluation into AI agent evaluation. Visit arena.dualmindlab.tech." width="413"></picture></a>
<a href="https://docs.dualmindlab.tech"><picture><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/harshbhx/harshbhx/main/assets/arena-figure-dark.svg"><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)" srcset="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/harshbhx/harshbhx/main/assets/arena-figure-light.svg"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/harshbhx/harshbhx/main/assets/arena-figure-dark.svg" alt="Fig. 2 — How a battle works, drawn as a request path: 1. User prompt (one real prompt, two models) → 2. Cloudflare CDN (absorbs traffic spikes) → 3. .NET Web API (stateless · scales out) → 4. Cloudflare AI Gateway (rate limits · cache · logs) → 5. Model A / Model B (identities hidden) → 6. Community vote (on the two answers) → 7. Supabase · PostgreSQL (the live leaderboard). Why it is built this way: CDN first, stateless API — Spikes land on Cloudflare, not the origin; scaling the .NET API out is a config change. AI Gateway over direct calls — One place for rate limits, caching and per-request logs across every model provider. Supabase on purpose — Leaderboard ranking needs relational queries. Names are revealed only after the vote. Docs: docs.dualmindlab.tech." width="413"></picture></a>
</p>

<a href="https://github.com/harshbhx/modvigil"><picture><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/harshbhx/harshbhx/main/assets/feature-modvigil-dark.svg"><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)" srcset="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/harshbhx/harshbhx/main/assets/feature-modvigil-light.svg"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/harshbhx/harshbhx/main/assets/feature-modvigil-dark.svg" alt="Feature No. 02: ModVigil — Reddit moderation automation · Devvit. Turns a subreddit’s raw mod log into a live dashboard and runs the routine safety work automatically — humans still make every final call. Fig. 4, rules in force (all switched on): Spike alerts — modmail when removals hit 3× the hourly baseline (checked every 15 min); Progressive warnings — educational note → final warning → flagged for human review; Ghost-mod detection — surfaces moderators inactive for 30+ days; Weekly digest — week-over-week report every Monday. Stack: Reddit Devvit, TypeScript, React, Redis. Link: github.com/harshbhx/modvigil." width="413"></picture></a>
</p>

Ship early: Real users surface problems planning never will. 2. Observability is architecture: If you can’t see it in production, it isn’t done. 3. Pick the right tool: The trade-off matters more than familiarity. 4. Own the outcome: The deliverable is the running, monitored system — not the commit. 5. Communicate clearly: Async first, unprompted updates, no surprises. — Harsh, Vadodara, India." width="413"></picture>
</p>

**No. 1 — The Arena story: DualMind Arena** (live at [arena.dualmindlab.tech](https://arena.dualmindlab.tech))

Public AI benchmarks are easy to game: cherry-picked prompts, brand bias, results nobody can audit. Two models answer the same real prompt with their names hidden; the community votes before the identities are revealed, and the votes feed a live leaderboard.

- **5,000+** requests absorbed in one traffic spike — Bots + real users; Cloudflare CDN took the load before it reached the origin.
- **#1** on Google for “DualMind Labs” — dualmindlab.tech
- **Real-time** login anomaly detection — IP capture, risk scoring and an email alert to the account owner on every suspicious event.
- **Docs** full user documentation, published — docs.dualmindlab.tech
- **CDN first, stateless API:** Spikes land on Cloudflare, not the origin; scaling the .NET API out is a config change.
- **AI Gateway over direct calls:** One place for rate limits, caching and per-request logs across every model provider.
- **Supabase on purpose:** Leaderboard ranking needs relational queries.
- **Stack:** Azure, .NET Web API, Vanilla JS, Supabase · PostgreSQL, Cloudflare CDN, Cloudflare AI Gateway, GitHub Actions
- **Request path:** User prompt → Cloudflare CDN → .NET Web API (stateless) → Cloudflare AI Gateway (rate limits · cache · logs) → Model A / Model B (identities hidden) → Community vote → Supabase · PostgreSQL (leaderboard)
- **Next:** Expanding from model evaluation into AI agent evaluation.

**No. 2 — Selected work**

- **PixelProof** — Chrome extension · AI image detection · built for Next Byte Hacks V2 — [pixelproof.dualmindlab.tech](https://pixelproof.dualmindlab.tech) · [Devpost](https://devpost.com/software/pixelproof-l5ofpx) · [Source](https://github.com/harshbhx/pixelproof)
  - Flags AI-generated and manipulated images on any page, explains the verdict in plain English and cross-checks the claim against live fact-check data.
  - Detect (Reality Defender API) → Explain (Google Gemini, in plain English) → Cross-check (Google Fact Check API)
  - **Stack:** Chrome MV3, Vanilla JS, Gemini, Reality Defender, Fact Check API
- **ModVigil** — Reddit moderation automation · Devvit · built for Reddit Mod Tools Hackathon 2026 — [Source](https://github.com/harshbhx/modvigil)
  - Turns a subreddit’s raw mod log into a live dashboard and runs the routine safety work automatically — humans still make every final call.
  - **Spike alerts:** modmail when removals hit 3× the hourly baseline (checked every 15 min)
  - **Progressive warnings:** educational note → final warning → flagged for human review
  - **Ghost-mod detection:** surfaces moderators inactive for 30+ days
  - **Weekly digest:** week-over-week report every Monday
  - **Stack:** Reddit Devvit, TypeScript, React, Redis
- **AI Component Builder** — Generative UI · Cursor SDK · built for Cursor workshop, Rajkot — [Source](https://github.com/harshbhx/cursor-rajkot-workshop)
  - A chat panel streams generated React components from the Cursor SDK into a live preview with syntax-highlighted code.
  - Prompt (chat panel) → Generate (Cursor SDK, streamed over SSE) → Preview (sandboxed iframe + code view)
  - **Stack:** Next.js 14, TypeScript, Cursor SDK, SSE, Tailwind
- **AI Support Agent** — Support automation · function calling
  - Claude / GPT-4o with function calling classifies every inbound query by intent and urgency, resolves the routine ones and escalates the rest with the context already drafted.
  - Classify (intent + urgency) → Resolve (auto-reply, logged to the CRM) → Escalate (human review, context pre-drafted)
  - **Stack:** Node.js, Claude, GPT-4o, Supabase, Webhooks
- **MealMind** — Restaurant ecosystem · 3 Flutter apps
  - Customer, chef and admin apps on one Firebase backend: a confirmed Razorpay payment reaches the kitchen screen and the admin dashboard in under a second.
  - Pay (Razorpay, in the customer app) → Confirm (webhook → Cloud Function) → Sync (one Firestore write, every app)
  - **Stack:** Flutter ×3, Firestore, Firebase Auth, Cloud Functions, Razorpay

_House rules_

1. **Ship early.** Real users surface problems planning never will.
2. **Observability is architecture.** If you can’t see it in production, it isn’t done.
3. **Pick the right tool.** The trade-off matters more than familiarity.
4. **Own the outcome.** The deliverable is the running, monitored system — not the commit.
5. **Communicate clearly.** Async first, unprompted updates, no surprises.
